fact_check_verdict: Publish as a live local process story. The Nov 2 reading outcome is unreported. No source says what Petersburg's facility would compute; AI appears only in the original vendor's own marketing.

claims.spoken: On November second, Petersburg's Assembly took up a temporary pause on data center permits.
claims.on_screen: NOV 2 · ASSEMBLY TAKES UP A PAUSE
requires: KFSK previewed the meeting. The outcome was not reported as of November 7th. Never say it passed.

claims.spoken: The proposed pause would run through September of next year.
It targets data centers that would exceed grid capacity, rely on generators, or use uncontained cooling.
claims.on_screen: OVER GRID CAPACITY · GENERATORS · UNCONTAINED COOLING

claims.spoken: November second was only the first of three readings.
requires: Need two more readings to become law.

claims.spoken: Petersburg has no data center today.
In September the planning commission asked for a one year pause to study the impacts.
On September twenty first the Assembly tied three to three on it, so it failed.
requires: The Assembly tied, not the Planning Commission.

claims.spoken: Mayor Bob Lynn said he couldn't support a moratorium.
claims.on_screen: "I CAN'T SUPPORT A MORATORIUM." · MAYOR BOB LYNN

claims.spoken: Vice Mayor Jeigh Stanton Gregor called it a solution in search of a problem.
claims.on_screen: "A SOLUTION IN SEARCH OF A PROBLEM" · JEIGH STANTON GREGOR

claims.spoken: Rob Schwartz said pause it a little bit.
claims.on_screen: "PAUSE IT A LITTLE BIT." · ROB SCHWARTZ

claims.spoken: On October fifth the Assembly unanimously approved a nine month pause to be drafted.
requires: Cite October 16th article.

claims.spoken: Stanton Gregor said it had been a pretty divisive issue and he'd love to find consensus.
claims.on_screen: "I'D LOVE TO FIND CONSENSUS." · STANTON GREGOR
requires: Quote is from the October 16th article.

claims.spoken: The Assembly also unanimously started work on zoning rules.
The site is the old Ocean Beauty cannery.
requires: Per the utility's FAQ.

claims.spoken: A private company, Mazzella Alaska, owns the cannery's two megawatt transformer.
requires: Per the utility's FAQ.

claims.spoken: The building would be fifteen hundred to two thousand square feet.
requires: Per the utility's FAQ.

claims.spoken: The first plan, from a vendor called Greensparc, was one megawatt using eight and a half million kilowatt hours a year.
requires: Per the utility's April FAQ. Greensparc deal later did not finalize.

claims.spoken: At the full two megawatts, seventeen million kilowatt hours a year.
requires: Per the utility's FAQ.

claims.spoken: The whole cannery used one million sixty four thousand kilowatt hours in 2015.
requires: Per the utility's FAQ. Do not say peak.

claims.spoken: So the full build would use about sixteen times the cannery.
requires: Derived from the FAQ figures c18 and c19, 15.97.

claims.spoken: The utility says residential power costs twelve point two cents a kilowatt hour.
requires: Per the utility's FAQ.

claims.spoken: The utility puts the Alaska average near thirty cents.
requires: Per the utility's FAQ. Not cross-checked against EIA.

claims.spoken: The utility estimates over two million dollars a year in revenue.
requires: Per the utility's FAQ. KFSK May 1st reported one to two million.

claims.spoken: The utility says the data center would lessen planned rate increases.
requires: Per the utility's FAQ.

claims.spoken: The plan had no diesel generators on site, only batteries for controlled shutdowns.
claims.on_screen: NO DIESEL GENERATORS ON SITE · BATTERIES
requires: Per the utility's FAQ. Town grid has diesel backup.

claims.spoken: Cooling was to be a closed loop, like a car radiator.
requires: Per the utility's FAQ.

claims.spoken: The Greensparc deal didn't finalize, but the owner is still pursuing a small project.
requires: Per KFSK. No new partner named.

claims.spoken: Greensparc's own website markets high density AI compute.
requires: Vendor marketing only. Not a statement about what Petersburg would run. No source says what Petersburg would compute.
